title: Uniform Initialization and Type Deduction
learningObjectives: Explain the main ideas of Uniform Initialization and Type Deduction.
Identify the language rules and relevant C++ constructs.
Apply the topic in a small program.
Recognize common pitfalls and safety concerns.
Test an example and justify design decisions.

understand.concept: Brace initialization uses {} and can reject narrowing. auto deduces a type from its initializer. Be careful: initializer-list constructors affect overload selection; vector braces and parentheses mean different things.
understand.whyItMatters: Clear initialization prevents accidental conversions and uninitialized variables; type deduction reduces verbosity when readable.
understand.explain: Prefer braces where they improve safety. Use auto when deduction is obvious, otherwise explicit types. Know vector braces-versus-parentheses semantics.
